name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 1, 2015

 A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
 Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
 Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
 Pro Tem Raths at 5:00 p.m., on June 1, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

 A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
 by 5:00 p.m. on May 29, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
 posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
 Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

 *All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Raths declared a recess. The City Council reconvened
at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council did not hold a closed session this
evening.

City Council Minutes  1  June 1, 2015
 INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Schlicht

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim the Month of June "RELAY FOR LIFE and Paint our Town Purple
  Month"

  Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to American Cancer Society Community
  Manager Megan Pierce, Event Lead/Volunteer Denise Matson, and Volunteer Steve Bell.

 PUBLIC COMMENTS

 Jeff Snow, Regional Leadership Council Member for the Special Olympics of Southern
 California: thanked the City of Mission Viejo for participating as a Special Olympics World
 Games Host Town.

 Doug McClintock, M.V.: informed the City Council of a sport called "pop tennis" and requested
 that the Council consider dedicating space for the development of public courts.

 Jim Flynn, M.V.: invited the City Council Members to upcoming Chamber of Commerce events
 including the monthly mixer, ribbon cutting ceremonies and weekly meetings.

 Kathy Richardson, M.V.: shared video of her car being hit on the street in front of her home by
 a distracted driver who was on the phone at the time.

 Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: outlined programs that will be held at the Murray Community Center in
 June, July, and August and she encouraged residents to pick up a copy of the class listings. Mrs.
 Boyce also announced that she is a member of the Senior Citizens Advisory Council which
 meets every month at the community center. Their primary concern is helping seniors,
 legislatively, to lead a much better life and she invited the Council Members and Commissioners
 to attend the next meeting on Friday, June 12 at 9:30 a.m.

 Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the City's recent transaction to sell a piece of property to
 the Housing Authority likens Mission Viejo to the city of Bell.

 CONSENT CALENDAR

 Items 6, 7, 8, and 13 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

 Mayor Schlicht announced that she has asked the City Clerk to make a minor addition to her
 Council Comments (page 13) for the May 18 meeting.

City Council Minutes  2  June 1, 2015
  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the Consent
 Calendar as outlined below.
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

 AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
 NOES:  None
 ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 18, 2015, as amended.

3.  Check Register Dated May 8, 2015 in the Amount of $648,216.42

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated May 15, 2015 in the Amount of $918,272.34

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre – Year 2015 – Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 15-23 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt on
  Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City Council
  to Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for Hearing
  Protests; (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to Destroy Weeds
  in accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3) instructed the City
  Clerk to set the Public Hearing for August 25, 2015.

9.  Annual Routine Janitorial and Related Services at Various Park Sites and Facilities

  (1) Approved the Fifth Amendment for the Annual Routine Janitorial and Related Services
  at Various Park Sites and Facilities contract to Vocational Visions for the period of July 1,
  2015, to June 30, 2017, in an amount not to exceed $254,914.80; and (2) authorized staff
  to issue a purchase order to Vocational Visions for the period of July 1, 2015, through June
  30, 2016, in an amount not to exceed $127,457.40, pending adoption of the 2015-17 budget
  by the City Council.

10.  Microsoft Licensing Renewal

City Council Minutes  3  June 1, 2015
   Approved the three-year agreement with Microsoft for Microsoft Product Licensing
  renewal and authorized issuance of a purchase order to CompuCom for such services for
  2015-16 in the amount of $65,440.52.

11.  Update the City of Mission Viejo Natural Hazards Mitigation Plan with Corrections

  Rescinded Resolution 15-17, and adopted Resolution 15-24 Approving the City of Mission
  Viejo Natural Hazards Mitigation Plan.

12.  First Amendment to the Mission Viejo Library Materials Purchasing and Processing
  Agreement

  (1) Approved the First Amendment to the Mission Viejo Library Materials Purchasing and
  Processing Agreement with Baker and Taylor, Inc., for the period of July 1, 2015, through
  June 30, 2017, in the amount of $400,000; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order
  to Baker and Taylor, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2015, through June 30, 2016, in an
  amount not to exceed $200,000 pending adoption of the 2015-17 budget by the City
  Council.

14.  2015 Residential Resurfacing– CDBG Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)
  – Award of Contract

  (1) Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to R. J. Noble Company in
  the amount of $5,087,000.00; and (2) adopted Resolution 15-26 Amending the Fiscal Year
  2014-2015 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Project 838.

OLD BUSINESS

16.  Marguerite Aquatics Complex Needs Assessment Review

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of the refurbishment of the Marguerite Aquatics Complex:
  Jay Standish, M.V.; Ed Tutton, M.V.; Leo Martinez, M.V.; Marty Nohe, M.V.; Diane
  Galaz-Campbell, M.V.; Art Villalovos, M.V.; Stephen Barnes, Trabuco Canyon.; Richard
  Munro, M.V.; Arthur Cook, M.V.; Mark Jones, M.V.; Clayton "C.J." Smith, M.V.; Brian
  Goodell, M.V.; Judy Bullockus, M.V.; Ruth Boersma, M.V.; Rhonda Reardon, M.V.; Head
  Coach Bill Rose, Nadadores, M.V.; Janet Ely, High Performance Director, Nadadores Dive
  Team, Rancho Santa Margarita; Coach Jacqueline O'Hagan, Nadadores, M.V.; Avery
  Ackerman and Haley Badger, M.V.; Coach Ryan Cox, Nadadores, San Juan Capistrano;
  Cami Hidalgo, M.V.; Colten Young, Trabuco Canyon.; Robert Banis, MV.; Coach T.
  Sorenson, Nadadores, M.V.; Brian Clark, Laguna Niguel; Coach Cindy Adams, Novice
  Director of the Nadadores Dive Team, M.V.; Kim Barnes, Nadadores Foundation Member,
  M.V.; Greg Louganis via a video recording, Beverly Hills; Mark Gohr, Nadadores
  Foundation Member, Laguna Niguel; Sara Gilliland, M.V.; Tom Ashbrook, President of

City Council Minutes  4  June 1, 2015
   the Nadadores Foundation, Rancho Santa Margarita; Roger Young, Vice President of the
  Nadadores Foundation, Trabuco Canyon; Casey Cooper, Ph.D. M.V.

  The following spoke in opposition to the dive tower replacement unless a survey is done
  on the dive tower needs: Gail Reavis, M.V.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:19 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:29
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  the Community Services Commission option 3, without the solar thermal panels, and
  require the Nadadores to provide the City with a Promissory Note for their $1.3 million
  commitment.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to call the
  question and end the debate.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  Annual Routine Park, Right-of-Way, and Facility Electrical, Lighting Maintenance
  Repair and Replacement

  Council Member Sachs asked if the $489,000 referred to in the staff report is being added
  to a base contract amount and what that amount is.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that the
  proposed is a one-time two year contract renewal in the amount of $489,000.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  approve First Amendment to the existing contract with C & D Electric for the period July
  1, 2015 through June 30, 2017 to increase the contract amount by an amount not to exceed
City Council Minutes  5  June 1, 2015
   $489,000.00; and (2) authorize staff to issue a purchase order to C & D Electric for the
  period July 1, 2015 through June 30, 2016 in an amount not to exceed $244,500.00 pending
  adoption of the Fiscal Year 2015-2017 budget by the City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

7.  Annual Routine Street Sweeping Services

  Council Member Sachs asked for clarification on the percentages referred to in the staff
  report and what is the process for advising the City Council when the City Manager
  approves additional work.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1)
  approve First Amendment to the existing contract with Sunset Property Services for the
  period of July 1, 2015, through June 30, 2017, in an amount not to exceed $671,168.00,
  and (2) authorize staff to issue a purchase order to Sunset Property Services in an amount
  not to exceed $335,584.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Annual Road and Flood Control Maintenance Contract

  Council Member Sachs referenced his questions for item 7 and noted that his questions on
  this agenda item were essentially the same.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, (1) Approve
  County Agreement D14-077 with the County of Orange for the period July 1, 2015,
  through June 30, 2017 in the amount of $1,975,224.00; and (2) authorize issuance of a
  purchase order to the County of Orange for the period of July 1, 2015 through June 30,
  2016 in an amount not to exceed $987,612.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  June 1, 2015
 13.  2014 Residential Resurfacing-CDBG Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP
  838)-Notice of Completion

  There were no questions on item 13.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1) certify
  the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize the
  City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record the
  Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance
  and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the
  Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and (4)
  authorize the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice
  of Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

15.  FY 2015-16 Law Enforcement Services Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange Cou

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Lt. Brad NewMyer presented details on the department's statistics and goals.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed concern that staff has not met with other cities on
  police cost savings measures.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  approve the FY 2015-16 Law Enforcement Services Agreement (A15-31) with the County
  of Orange for an amount not to exceed $17,546,055; and (2) authorize the City Manager to
  approve reimbursements related to special enforcement services in an amount not to exceed
  $65,000 for FY 2015-16.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  June 1, 2015
 NEW BUSINESS

17.  Payment Toward the Pension Unfunded Liabilities

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  direct staff to issue a check to the California Public Employees Retirement System
  (CalPERS) in the amount of $1,500,000 toward the pension unfunded liability; and (2)
  adopt Resolution 15-25 Amending the FY 2014/15 Budget to Appropriate Resources for
  Payment Towards Unfunded Liabilities.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Santa Margarita Water District’s Drought Response Ad Hoc Committee

  *Note: City Council approval of the Minutes on June 15, 2015, included direction to insert
  a verbatim transcript for this agenda item.

  City Manager Wilberg: Santa Margarita Water District sent an e-mail requesting… they
  are forming an ad hoc committee to discuss the district's drought response and they asked
  the City to appoint two members to that committee. Actually, this is something… we've
  been meeting with the various districts ever since the Governor's emergency proclamation.
  And what's important for the City of Mission Viejo is that we have as consistent a message
  as we can, especially since we are served by four different water districts and they all have
  different policies in place. And so the idea here is that this committee has the opportunity
  to develop a consistent and carefully crafted clear message to the residents so they know
  what the requirements are for each different water district. So, they made a request that
  the City appoint two council members to be a part of that committee to help formulate
  those various messages in response to the drought situation.

  Mayor Schlicht: I'm gonna jump in here first. Well, first of all there is a, what I consider
  a Brown Act violation, Mr. City Manager, when you shared my comments that I had with
  Mr. Leach. You sent it out and then there were two Council Members that came forward
  and made a determination basically. But I think the public needs to have an
  understanding on my position and why I declined the invitation. And I'll just read that e-
  mail that I had forwarded to the City Manager. I said, uh – and this e-mail went out to
  Mr. Bill Curley, Mr. Dennis Wilberg, Karen Hamman, Keith Rattay, Greg… and here we

City Council Minutes  8  June 1, 2015
   go. It says, "Hello, all. In talking with Mr. Leach, I declined our participation on its
  honorary ad hoc committee. He lost me when he said ‘lockstep’ and ‘representing
  committee to the larger Council.’ I thanked him and stated that in talking with our City
  Attorney, Bill Curley, we'll be creating our own water committee. I based my comment
  on the fact that we have three water districts in the City and having our own committee…
  our committee would be representing the entire City. An invitation was extended to him
  for the Santa Margarita Water District representation on our committee.” And I
  concluded by, "I look forward to us being a leader on conservation measures, creating a
  model for our residents and the HOAs." Um, so, that, that was my position. I don't think
  it's right for one water district to be wanting us to walk lockstep, and that was Mr. Leach's
  direct comment to me - that we have to, you know, the other water districts follow in
  style like that. So, it's my position, and it was a great opportunity that Mr. Curley had
  stated, and we had talked briefly about it, and I think I mentioned in a prior Council
  meeting, that we start our own water committee. And that's the direction I would prefer,
  so I'd like to make a motion… well, I guess we have some comments first. Um, I'll just
  make a…. I don't want a second right now until we have everybody's comments. But my
  desire would be to create our own water committee, invite the other water districts to join
  us, and then we can collaboratively create a program that would be evenly enforced or
  shared city-wide. So Mr. Greg Raths.

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths: Madam Mayor, do we not have our own ad hoc water committee
  that Steve Spillman chairs?

  Council Member Ury: At the Planning and Transportation Commission we do.

  Mayor Schlicht: That was what, Frank?

  Council Member Ury: At the Planning and Transportation Commission they have
  already created their own water subcommittee.

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths: Right. 'Cause he's spoken to me. Him and I have been to Santa
  Margarita Water twice talking with them. So, I would like to continue that relationship.
  We're making…. we're not gonna be in anyone's lockstep. We're going to do what’s best
  for Mission Viejo.

  Mayor Schlicht: Well, well, that's different from what this committee is. So, if that,
  that's going on, that's fine.

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths: Right. We do have a committee but… I would like to be in there
  just to see what Santa Margarita Water has to do because we have a lot of influence under
  their water district. So, even – I'm not gonna be in their lockstep – if you put me on that
  committee. I'd like to be on it. I'm not gonna step in anyone's lockstep. I'll step into
  what's best for the City. So…

  Mayor Schlicht: Very good. Wendy, you had comments next.

City Council Minutes  9  June 1, 2015
   Council Member Bucknum: I just have a question on the request to have us on there, on
  the committee, and how that is under the, I mean that… I guess I'm a little bit confused
  because, in the spirit of transparency, how come it didn't come before the City Council to
  decide whether we would or wouldn't be on this honorary committee, or whatever it is?

  Mayor Schlicht: It was presented to me and I've made the follow-up phone call. So…

  Council Member Bucknum: Okay. Well, you're the one who wants transparency, so
  why wouldn't it have come here?

  Mayor Schlicht: Because what… well, transparency means we include all the water
  district facilities that are in our City. So, my response was, instead of walking lockstep,
  which was Mr. Leach's comments to me – and he agreed with me. He was happy to join
  our committee so, I wanted to take the leadership role. That's what my position was and I
  think as Mayor, I'm not abusing my position at all. I was making it a City-wide
  committee versus just one water district. Um, Frank, you had some comments.

  Council Member Ury: Just a couple quick things. When these types of invitations are
  brought up it's customary for the Mayor to put them on the agenda before making a
  unilateral decision. In addition, part of what's important now is that every water
  district… I mean, having the water district take the lead does not take away from the
  work that we will be doing as a City. It will simply be integrating us into whatever
  they're doing on their side. In the same way that we don't ask water districts to join us to
  discuss transportation or infrastructure, it's definitely appropriate that they take the lead.
  Now, if they don't meet – you know, as Mayor Pro Tem Raths mentioned – if they don't
  meet our goals we can certainly do what we can to influence them and won't take their
  words, you know, lockstep. However, thinking that we have the policy people in place to
  lead the discussion in a holistic sense… both in terms of conservation, which is candidly
  one of the only areas that we can really influence it very much, but in terms of water
  generation, recycling, reuse… and to put all those things in place, we're gonna be
  basically communicating with all the different water districts. So that's why, as we go
  forward, we do need to be participating in all these you know, going forward. And that's
  why I like the idea of having this Council discuss whether or not we want to participate.
  Thank you.

  Mayor Schlicht: Okay. Well, I just want to remind everybody that this was an honorary
  ad hoc. We were not asked to participate. It was honorary, and to take back the
  commission’s responses back to the bigger committee. So, we were just… it was an
  honorary position, and as Mission Viejo Mayor, I would… don't… you know, am I
  supposed to feel honored to be on their… you know, to take their instruction? No. That's
  why I had responded and Mr. Leach was very understanding and actually agreed with me
  that it would be better to have our own committee with their representation coming to us.
  So it was a leadership role that I did take. I know that you don't see it that way. And
  everybody knows if I say it's white the bookends will say it's black. Anyways, and I also
  want to remind some of our Council members who were at that – I forget what it was
  called. It was in January, Economic Coalition Meeting… “Libations with Legislatures” I
City Council Minutes  10  June 1, 2015
   think. It was Mr. Leach that, you know, said that they were the anti-NIMBY group and
  were here to infill our communities. So, I don't believe that, you know, Mr. Leach is a
  good representative for us and I just would prefer that we sit in the driver's seat. We
  invite them to offer what their plans are, and we can coordinate it with all the other water
  districts. Does anybody want…oh, Mr. Sachs.

  Council Member Sachs: Thank you. Quite honestly, staff, I'm at a loss here because
  none of this information is on our iPads, so I can't refer back to the letter that was sent at
  all.

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths: You want mine?

  Mayor Schlicht: It's not on mine. I've got nothing… So, why don't we postpone this two
  weeks.

  Council Member Sachs: That's what I was going to ask. Is this an urgent appointment?

  City Manager Wilberg: No. And it's not as ominous as it's being made out to be. So it
  can certainly be delayed two weeks. I'll ask Jim Leach to come personally and explain
  his thoughts on what they're gonna do. It's really just to get thoughts from…. You’ll
  read, he wants to “pull together a committee of representatives. It's a City that we serve,
  so we're soliciting Mission Viejo, Rancho Santa Margarita, and San Clemente.” And
  they also plan to include Supervisor Bartlett. The idea is just being able to make sure that
  their message is being communicated the same way in all the cities. So, I'll invite him to
  come to your next Council meeting under presentations.

  Council Member Sachs: Yeah. If we could table this Council, I would certainly like to
  do that 'cause I'm, I'm kind of in the dark here. Um, so, if…

  Mayor Schlicht:  Okay. Do we need to vote to table or do we just table?

  City Attorney Curley: You've declared your consensus. Everybody nods… close enough.

  Mayor Schlicht: Okay. Yeah, ‘cause we have got a lot more to do yet. Okay. So, that's
  tabled. Now we're on to number 19.

19.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report / AB1217 (Daly)

  City Manager Wilberg provided an update on the movement of AB1217 in the Assembly
  and on to the Senate Committee.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the Orange County Employee Retirement System
  (OCERS) is aware of the heightened threat of OCFA member withdrawals and the potential
  for an OCFA bankruptcy. He stated that he is very pleased by recent OCFA Board of
  Directors actions with reform-minded individuals voicing vigorous opposition to a union

City Council Minutes  11  June 1, 2015
   proposal to reduce the board size. Finally, Mr. Wontrobski asked Council Member Sachs,
  as an OCFA Board Member, to obtain copies of records that he has requested from OCFA
  free of charge so he doesn't have to pay $136 for them.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to direct the City
  Manager to immediately contact other South Orange County city managers to ascertain
  whether there is interest and/or support in developing a South Orange County exploratory
  group of city managers to convene and discuss, evaluate and examine options for the 5th
  district cities for collective withdrawal from the OCFA.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

20.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the OCTA
  Board of Directors.

STAFF REPORTS

21.  Proposed 2015-17 Budget for the City of Mission Viejo

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented an outline and Director of Administrative
  Services Cheryl Dyas presented a high-level summary of the proposed budget.

 At the hour of 10:16 p.m., Council Member Sachs vacated the dais.

 RECESS

 At the hour of 10:18 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
 10:24 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

22.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

 Council Member Bucknum

 Council Member Bucknum encouraged everyone to support the City's Relay for Life June 6-7,
 2015. She congratulated Nadadores Katie McLaughlin and Grant Shoults who were awarded
City Council Minutes  12  June 1, 2015
  "Swimmer of the Year" by the Orange County Register. Council Member Bucknum thanked her
 colleagues for their vote tonight on the Marguerite Aquatics Complex which, she stated, is a
 very important part of Mission Viejo's heritage.

 Council Member Sachs

 Council Member Sachs announced that he had nothing to report.

 Council Member Ury

 Council Member Ury stated that he had nothing to report.

 Mayor Pro Tem Raths

 Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked Assemblyman Bill Brough for appointing him to a Veterans
 Advisory Committee.

 Mayor Schlicht

 Mayor Schlicht stated that it was a hard no vote on the Nadadores complex but she doesn't
 believe that the taxpayers should be responsible for all that they are burdened with now. She
 noted that the Nadadores are part of the City's heritage, as are all sports. Mayor Schlicht
 announced that she has been invited by Roger Marsh to appear on a radio talk show to speak
 about the Rotary's Prayer Breakfast and the continuing trend to not allow conservative officials
 to be guest speakers. Lastly, Mayor Schlicht asked staff what is next with the Youth Center
 concept.

 City Manager Wilberg responded that the Community Services Commission will be addressing
 the matter tomorrow night.

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 10:28 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
 session, Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Monday, June 15, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________________
 Karen Hamman, City Clerk

 Approved at the meeting of June 15, 2015

City Council Minutes  13  June 1, 2015
